title: Network rules by app
noApps: No app has its own rules yet.
noMoreApps: Every app already has rules here.
precedence: There is no order to set: when several rules match a connection, the most specific one decides. An exact domain beats *.domain, a longer wildcard beats a shorter one, an address beats its network, and any of them beats the app's default. With equally specific rules, the one with a port beats any port, a protocol beats any protocol, and Block beats Allow. The list shows each app's rules in that order.
dnsNote: Domains are matched with the names the system resolver returned for each address. An app that uses its own encrypted DNS (for example DNS over HTTPS inside a browser) asks without the system, so its names can't be matched: a domain rule doesn't see those connections, while address and network rules, the app's default and its restrictions still apply.
default.allowHint: What no rule covers follows the firewall mode.
default.denyHint: Only what an Allow rule covers can connect.
notEnforceable: This app has no scope of its own (it was not opened from Axia DE), so its rules are kept but not enforced.
meaning.wildcard: {name} and every name under it (www.{name}, a.b.{name}…).
meaning.lan: Every local address (the LAN, this computer).
field.dstHint: A domain (example.com), every subdomain (*.example.com), an address (192.0.2.7) or a network (10.0.0.0/8, 2001:db8::/32).
field.portHint: Empty for any; one (443) or a range (8000-8080).
err.domain: Not a valid domain: letters, digits, hyphens and dots, labels up to 63 characters. International names go in punycode (xn--…).
err.wildcard: A wildcard is written *. and a domain, such as *.example.com.
err.address: Not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
err.prefix: The prefix after / must be 0–32 for IPv4 or 0–128 for IPv6.
err.hostBits: The address has bits set outside the prefix: write the network's first address (for example 10.0.0.0/8).
err.isDefault: A rule for every destination is the app's default: set it above.
err.port: Ports go from 1 to 65535; a range is low-high.
err.save: The rule could not be saved.
sheet.nameNote: The name is the one the system resolver returned for this connection's address.
sheet.noName: The system resolver reported no name for this address (or the app found it with its own DNS), so the rule is prefilled with the address. You can type a domain instead.
pickAddress: Select an address to allow or block it for this app.
